difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 620-637: when substituting a deduction N of A for x in M produces a redex and M is not the variable x, the redex arises in one of four enumerated ways, and the cut rank of the substituted deduction is either the cut rank of M or the length of A. The author proof (638-663) runs induction on M, working the variable case, the redex-preserving cases and the conjunction-elimination cases in full detail with the displayed computations of the substituted deductions and their cut ranks, and finally covers the remaining elimination and application cases by the explicitly declared mirror argument. The case bookkeeping against the four-clause statement is real proof-theoretic work.
